text:
Alex DeBrincat scored his 300th career goal with 17 seconds left in the third period, a power-play strike that tied the game 3-3 and sent Detroit into overtime after it had trailed by three. Seattle finished the job in a shootout, with Bobby McMann beating Daniil Tarasov in the fourth round and Dylan Larkin unable to answer, giving the Kraken a 4-3 win at Climate Pledge Arena.

For two periods, Seattle controlled it. Mackie Samoskevich opened the scoring in the first, Ryker Evans added a power-play goal early in the second, and Brandon Montour made it 3-0 late in that period. Seattle also led the chance quality (expected goals, a measure of how good each team's shots were) 1.37 to 0.52 in the second. Then the game flipped. Detroit out-chanced the Kraken 1.58 to 0.56 in the third. Viktor Arvidsson scored on a 4% look, Lucas Raymond scored on the power play a minute later, and DeBrincat's goal, set up by Larkin and Raymond, completed the rally. Detroit also took 74 shot attempts to Seattle's 54, though Philipp Grubauer still faced only 25 shots on goal.

Over the full game the numbers split almost evenly. Seattle had a slight edge, 2.70 expected goals to 2.56, and "deserved to win" (the share of simulated replays of every shot that a team wins) came out 53% for the Kraken and 47% for the Red Wings. In the earlier meeting this season, on October 9, Seattle won 6-3 in regulation. The facts here don't include standings or streaks for either team, but Seattle has now beaten Detroit both times, while the Red Wings leave with a point and a milestone goal from DeBrincat.
